## Audit result: no collateral loss is still outstanding

Enumerated every file `6125c5345f01` added and classified each against `9c7d78127696`'s removal. `6125c5345f01` touched 16 files (+2722/-43), and the revert was a true wholesale inverse of that delta. `git diff 6125c5345f01^ 9c7d78127696` is non-empty only because the revert was based on a later parent carrying unrelated E2E toolchain work.

### Classification

INTENDED (scanner-gate machinery, correctly removed with the gate) — 15 files: `.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml`, `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `Makefile`, `docs/security.md`, `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`, `infra/compose/review-scanners.linux-amd64.requirements.txt`, `infra/compose/review-scanners.linux-arm64.requirements.txt`, `infra/compose/review-scanners.lock.json`, `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`, `scripts/install_review_scanners.py`, `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py`, `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py`, `tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py`, `tests/unit/test_workflow_names.py`.

`scripts/gen_config_reference.py` was examined specifically, as the AC requires. Its hunk generated the `## Review scanner lock authority` security-reference section — documentation *for* the scanner lock machinery, not an independent config capability. Its removal was intended. The four test files were likewise read hunk-by-hunk rather than classified by filename; three of them assert scanner-specific wiring.

COLLATERAL — 1 file: `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py`. It carried the `# mechanism-ok:` contributor contract, which is independent of scanners: the committed-tree checks moved from `baseline == live` to `set(baseline) | admitted == live`, plus a coupled correction to the standalone bare-`pytest` import path.

### Current status on origin/main

Both losses have since been repaired, by two separate commits:

- `cf9c3daf992` "Make the mechanism-ok contract survive a revert" restored the mechanism-delta contract. `origin/main`'s `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` now holds 6 marker tests, including `test_a_marker_with_a_reason_admits_a_new_mechanism`, the parametrized `test_a_marker_without_a_real_reason_does_not_admit` over `["", "   "]`, and `test_a_marker_admits_only_the_mechanism_it_names` — which pins exactly the three properties this ticket asked about: a marker admits the `(kind, name)` it names, a blank reason is an error, and a marker is not a blanket opt-out for its kind. The committed-tree assertions consult `ratchet.markers_for` again.
- `4c994034814` "Reland scanner integration as advisory" restored the scanner machinery, this time advisory rather than a `Verified` requirement — which also resolves the original motivation for the revert.

### Verdict

The audit is clean. The mechanism-ok contract was the only collateral casualty, and it is no longer outstanding. Nothing needs re-applying, so there is no re-apply/leave-removed decision left to record.

On the last acceptance criterion — the general lesson — it was already acted on in the tree rather than only observed: `cf9c3daf992`'s subject is literally "Make the mechanism-ok contract survive a revert", and it added a source-level regression pin so the contract is no longer expressed only inside a feature commit. No further durable record is needed.

Closing as a clean audit with the enumeration above attached, so the next person does not re-run it.
